# Heat pump installer survey analysis

## Additional plots

### Foreword

As for all previous section, throughout the analysis, we collapsed responses and respondents to the survey into various subcategories to get the most relevant information. This collapsing was done based on the guidelines laid out in the [analysis plan](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M1nzdf3fyTjipmaKJKViin0EB3e3R1afOQglwMGJaII/edit){target="_blank"}.

You can find the pre-analysis code to run before analysing the installer survey below.

```{r}
# Link to the Miro board
# https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVNWK_xBg=/

# Link to the analysis plan
# https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M1nzdf3fyTjipmaKJKViin0EB3e3R1afOQglwMGJaII/edit#heading=h.voghu12g248q

##### Load packages
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(janitor)
library(wesanderson)
library(khroma)
library(RColorBrewer)

## Set working directory
setwd("C:\\Users\\benoit.siberdt\\Documents")

##### Load dataset
file_path <- "C:\\Users\\benoit.siberdt\\Documents\\20240201_Installer_survey_clean_data_anonymised.parquet"
Installer_survey_data <- arrow::read_parquet(file_path)

# Duplicate dataset to be sure not to mess it up
data_full <- tibble::tibble(Installer_survey_data)

##### Change names of variables to make things easier
data <- clean_names(data_full)

##### Recode free text answers
source("C:\\Users\\benoit.siberdt\\Downloads\\recode_variables.R")

##### Filter out partial responses
data <- data %>%
  filter(x0e_analytical_sample == "TRUE")

##### Pre-analysis - Collapsed options and new variables

## Create employment_type variables
data <- data %>%
  mutate(employment_type = case_when(x5_are_you_responding_to_this_survey_as == "An employee of a firm" ~ "Employee", 
                                     x5_are_you_responding_to_this_survey_as == "A contractor or freelancer" ~ "Contractor or freelancer",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I’m a sole trader" ~ "Sole trader",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with 5 or fewer employees" ~ "Company owner", 
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with 6-25 employees" ~ "Company owner",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with 26-100 employees" ~ "Company owner",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with over 100 employees" ~ "Company owner", TRUE ~ "Not asked"))
data$employment_type <- as.factor(data$employment_type)

# Create variable where employees and contractors are merged together
data <- data %>%
  mutate(employment_type_soletrader_owner_merged = case_when(employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ "Contractor or freelancer",
                                                             employment_type == "Employee" ~ "Employee",
                                                             employment_type == "Sole trader" ~ "Sole trader or company owner",
                                                             employment_type == "Company owner" ~ "Sole trader or company owner"))
data$employment_type_soletrader_owner_merged <- as.factor(data$employment_type_soletrader_owner_merged)

# Create variable where employees and contractors are merged together
data <- data %>%
  mutate(employment_type_employee_contractor_merged = case_when(employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ "Contractor/freelancer or employee",
                                                                employment_type == "Employee" ~ "Contractor/freelancer or employee",
                                                                employment_type == "Sole trader" ~ "Sole trader",
                                                                employment_type == "Company owner" ~ "Company owner"))
data$employment_type_employee_contractor_merged <- as.factor(data$employment_type_employee_contractor_merged)

# Create dummy variable for employment type
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_employment_type = case_when(employment_type == "Employee" ~ "Employee or contractor/freelancer",
                                           employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ "Employee or contractor/freelancer",
                                           employment_type == "Company owner" ~ "Company owner or sole trader",
                                           employment_type == "Sole trader" ~ "Company owner or sole trader"))
data$dummy_employment_type <- as.factor(data$dummy_employment_type)

# Create dummy for contractors and freelancers
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_contractors = case_when(employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0))

# Create dummy for employees
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_employees = case_when(employment_type == "Employee" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0))

# Create dummy for sole traders
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_soletraders = case_when(employment_type == "Sole trader" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0))

# Create dummy for company owner
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_company_owner = case_when(employment_type == "Company owner" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0))


##### Participant age
data <- data %>%
  mutate(age_collapsed = recode_factor(x1_how_old_are_you,
                                       "18-24" = "34 and under",
                                       "25-34" = "34 and under",
                                       "35-44" = "35-44",
                                       "45-54" = "45-54",
                                       "55-64" = "55 and over",
                                       "65-74" = "55 and over",
                                       "Over 75" = "55 and over",
                                       "Prefer not to say" = "Prefer not to say"))


##### Length of time in the heat pump sector
data <- data %>%
  mutate(length_hp_sector_collapsed = recode_factor(x4_how_long_have_you_been_working_with_heat_pumps,
                                                    "I don’t work with heat pumps, but plan to do so in the twelve months" = "Don’t work with heat pumps",
                                                    "I don’t work with heat pumps and have no plans to do so" = "Don’t work with heat pumps",
                                                    "Don't know" = "Don’t work with heat pumps",
                                                    "Less than 12 months" = "Under 3 years",
                                                    "1-3 years" = "Under 3 years",
                                                    "3-5 years" = "3-5 years",
                                                    "5-10 years" = "5-10 years",
                                                    "10-20 years" = "Over 10 years",
                                                    "Over 20 years" = "Over 10 years"))


##### Size of company owned
# Version 1
data <- data %>%
  mutate(size_company_owned_collapsed_1 = recode_factor(x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own,
                                                        "I’m a sole trader" = "Sole trader",
                                                        "I own a company with 5 or fewer employees" = "Small",
                                                        "I own a company with 6-25 employees" = "Medium",
                                                        "I own a company with 26-100 employees" = "Large",
                                                        "I own a company with over 100 employees" = "Large",
                                                        "Not asked" = "Not asked"))

# Version 2
data <- data %>%
  mutate(size_company_owned_collapsed_2 = recode_factor(x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own,
                                                        "I’m a sole trader" = "Sole trader",
                                                        "I own a company with 5 or fewer employees" = "Small",
                                                        "I own a company with 6-25 employees" = "Medium and large",
                                                        "I own a company with 26-100 employees" = "Medium and large",
                                                        "I own a company with over 100 employees" = "Medium and large",
                                                        "Not asked" = NA_character_))


##### Size of company employees work for
# Version 1
data <- data %>%
  mutate(size_company_employee_work_1 = recode_factor(x6b_what_size_company_do_you_work_for,
                                                      "I work for a company with 5 or fewer employees" = "5 or fewer",
                                                      "I work for a company with 6-25 employees" = "6-25",
                                                      "I work for a company with 26-100 employees" = "26-100",
                                                      "I work for a company with over 100 employees" = "Over 100",
                                                      "Not asked" = "Not asked",
                                                      "Don't know" = "Don't know"))

# Version 2
data <- data %>%
  mutate(size_company_employee_work_2 = recode_factor(x6b_what_size_company_do_you_work_for,
                                                      "I work for a company with 5 or fewer employees" = "25 or fewer",
                                                      "I work for a company with 6-25 employees" = "25 or fewer",
                                                      "I work for a company with 26-100 employees" = "Over 25",
                                                      "I work for a company with over 100 employees" = "Over 25",
                                                      "Not asked" = NA_character_,
                                                      "Don't know" = "Don't know"))



# Turn list into character so r can read the different answers
data$x8_answer1 <- sapply(data$x8_where_is_your_company_located, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x8_answer2 <- sapply(data$x8_where_is_your_company_located, function(x) as.character(x[2]))
data$x8_answer3 <- sapply(data$x8_where_is_your_company_located, function(x) as.character(x[3]))
data$x8_answer4 <- sapply(data$x8_where_is_your_company_located, function(x) as.character(x[4])) # No respondent selected more than 3 options for question 8
# Check answers using: table(data$answer)

# Create dummy for each possible option
# England
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_england = ifelse(str_detect(x8_answer1, "England") |
                                str_detect(x8_answer2, "England") |
                                str_detect(x8_answer3, "England"), 1, 0)) # 229

# Don't know
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_dont_know = ifelse(str_detect("Don't know", x8_answer1) |
                                  str_detect("Don't know", x8_answer2) |
                                  str_detect("Don't know", x8_answer3), 1, 0)) # 1

# I don't work in the UK
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_not_in_uk = ifelse(str_detect("I don't work in the UK", x8_answer1) |
                                  str_detect("I don't work in the UK", x8_answer2) |
                                  str_detect("I don't work in the UK", x8_answer3), 1, 0)) # 10

# Northern Ireland
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_northern_ireland = ifelse(str_detect("Northern Ireland", x8_answer1) |
                                         str_detect("Northern Ireland", x8_answer2) |
                                         str_detect("Northern Ireland", x8_answer3), 1, 0)) # 1

# Scotland
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_scotland = ifelse(str_detect("Scotland", x8_answer1) |
                                 str_detect("Scotland", x8_answer2) |
                                 str_detect("Scotland", x8_answer3), 1, 0)) # 41

# UK-wide business
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_uk_wide = ifelse(str_detect("UK-wide business", x8_answer1) |
                                str_detect("UK-wide business", x8_answer2) |
                                str_detect("UK-wide business", x8_answer3), 1, 0)) # 65

# Wales
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_wales = ifelse(str_detect("Wales", x8_answer1) |
                              str_detect("Wales", x8_answer2) |
                              str_detect("Wales", x8_answer3), 1, 0)) # 21


##### Distance travelled for work
data <- data %>%
  mutate(distance_travelled_for_work_collapsed = recode_factor(x10_how_far_from_your_business_location_would_you_typically_travel_for_jobs_approximately,
                                                               "Less than 25 miles" = "Less than 25 miles",
                                                               "25 to 50 miles" = "25-50 miles",
                                                               "50 to 100 miles" = "50-100 miles",
                                                               "100 to 200 miles" = "Over 100 miles",
                                                               "200 to 300 miles" = "Over 100 miles",
                                                               "More than 300 miles" = "Over 100 miles",
                                                               "Don't know" = "Don't know"))



## Domestic/commercial work split
# Company
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dom_com_work_plit_12a = recode_factor(x12a_thinking_of_your_companys_overall_heating_work_what_does_it_currently_consist_of,
                                               "Entirely domestic heating work, and no commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                               "Mostly domestic heating work, and some commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                               "An even amount of domestic and commercial heating work" = "Equal domestic/commercial",
                                               "Mostly commercial heating work, and some domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                               "Entirely commercial heating work, and no domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                               "Not asked" = "Not asked"))

# Individual
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dom_com_work_plit_12b = recode_factor(x12b_thinking_of_your_overall_heating_work_what_does_it_currently_consist_of,
                                               "Entirely domestic heating work, and no commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                               "Mostly domestic heating work, and some commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                               "An even amount of domestic and commercial heating work" = "Equal domestic/commercial",
                                               "Mostly commercial heating work, and some domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                               "Entirely commercial heating work, and no domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                               "Not asked" = "Not asked"))

## Merge variables for installers for q12
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x12a_bis = recode(x12a_thinking_of_your_companys_overall_heating_work_what_does_it_currently_consist_of, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x12b_bis = recode(x12b_thinking_of_your_overall_heating_work_what_does_it_currently_consist_of, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(x12_all = coalesce(x12a_bis, x12b_bis))


# Create collapse for q12 variable
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x12_all_collapsed = recode_factor(x12_all, 
                                             "Entirely domestic heating work, and no commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                             "Mostly domestic heating work, and some commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                             "An even amount of domestic and commercial heating work" = "Equal domestic/commercial",
                                             "Mostly commercial heating work, and some domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                             "Entirely commercial heating work, and no domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial"))


## Intentions for domestic/commercial work split
# Company
data <- data %>%
  mutate(intentions_dom_com_work_split_13a = recode_factor(x13a_thinking_of_your_companys_overall_heating_work_in_12_months_time_what_do_you_intend_it_to_consist_of,
                                                           "Entirely domestic heating work, and no commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                                           "Mostly domestic heating work, and some commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                                           "An even amount of domestic and commercial heating work" = "Equal domestic/commercial",
                                                           "Mostly commercial heating work, and some domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                                           "Entirely commercial heating work, and no domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                                           "Not asked" = "Not asked"))

# Individual
data <- data %>%
  mutate(intentions_dom_com_work_split_13b = recode_factor(x13b_thinking_of_your_overall_heating_work_in_12_months_time_what_do_you_intend_it_to_consist_of,
                                                           "Entirely domestic heating work, and no commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                                           "Mostly domestic heating work, and some commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                                           "An even amount of domestic and commercial heating work" = "Equal domestic/commercial",
                                                           "Mostly commercial heating work, and some domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                                           "Entirely commercial heating work, and no domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                                           "Not asked" = "Not asked"))


## Merge variables for installers for q13
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x13a_bis = recode(x13a_thinking_of_your_companys_overall_heating_work_in_12_months_time_what_do_you_intend_it_to_consist_of, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x13b_bis = recode(x13b_thinking_of_your_overall_heating_work_in_12_months_time_what_do_you_intend_it_to_consist_of, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(x13_all = coalesce(x13a_bis, x13b_bis))


# Create collapse for q13 variable
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x13_all_collapsed = recode_factor(x13_all, 
                                             "Entirely domestic heating work, and no commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                             "Mostly domestic heating work, and some commercial heating work" = "Mostly/entirely domestic",
                                             "An even amount of domestic and commercial heating work" = "Equal domestic/commercial",
                                             "Mostly commercial heating work, and some domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial",
                                             "Entirely commercial heating work, and no domestic heating work" = "Mostly/entirely commercial"))



## Ratio heating system installations that are heat pumps
# Company
data <- data %>%
  mutate(ratio_heating_systems_hp_company_14a = recode_factor(x14a_thinking_of_the_heating_systems_your_company_installs_do_you_work_on,
                                                              "Only heat pumps" = "Mostly heat pumps",
                                                              "Mostly heat pumps, and some other systems" = "Mostly heat pumps",
                                                              "An equal number of heat pumps and other systems" = "Equal split",
                                                              "Mostly other systems, and some heat pumps" = "Mostly non-heat pumps",
                                                              "Almost entirely other systems and the occasional heat pump" = "Mostly non-heat pumps",
                                                              "My company doesn't install any heat pumps, but plans to do so in the next 12 months" = "Don’t install heat pumps",
                                                              "My company doesn't install any heat pumps, and has no plans to do so" = "Don’t install heat pumps"))

# Individual
data <- data %>%
  mutate(ratio_heating_systems_hp_engineer_14b = recode_factor(x14b_thinking_of_the_heating_systems_you_install_do_you_work_on,
                                                               "Only heat pumps" = "Mostly heat pumps",
                                                               "Mostly heat pumps, and some other systems" = "Mostly heat pumps",
                                                               "An equal number of heat pumps and other systems" = "Equal split",
                                                               "Mostly other systems, and some heat pumps" = "Mostly non-heat pumps",
                                                               "Almost entirely other systems, and the occasional heat pump" = "Mostly non-heat pumps",
                                                               "I don't install any heat pumps, but I plan to do so in the next 12 months" = "Don’t install heat pumps",
                                                               "I don't install any heat pumps and have no plans to do so" = "Don’t install heat pumps"))

# Merge 14a and 14b (collapsed)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x14a_collapsed = recode(ratio_heating_systems_hp_company_14a, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x14b_collapsed = recode(ratio_heating_systems_hp_engineer_14b, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(x14_all_collapsed = coalesce(x14a_collapsed, x14b_collapsed))

# Merge 14a and 14b (not collapsed)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x14a_bis = recode(x14a_thinking_of_the_heating_systems_your_company_installs_do_you_work_on, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x14b_bis = recode(x14b_thinking_of_the_heating_systems_you_install_do_you_work_on, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(x14_all = coalesce(x14a_bis, x14b_bis))

data <- data %>%
  mutate(x14_all = case_when(x14_all == "Only heat pumps" ~ "Only heat pumps",
                             x14_all == "Mostly heat pumps, and some other systems" ~ "Mostly heat pumps, and some other systems",
                             x14_all == "An equal number of heat pumps and other systems" ~ "An equal number of heat pumps and other systems",
                             x14_all == "Mostly other systems, and some heat pumps" ~ "Mostly other systems, and some heat pumps",
                             x14_all == "Almost entirely other systems, and the occasional heat pump" ~ "Almost entirely other systems, and the occasional heat pump",
                             x14_all == "Almost entirely other systems and the occasional heat pump" ~ "Almost entirely other systems, and the occasional heat pump",
                             x14_all == "My company doesn't install any heat pumps, but plans to do so in the next 12 months" ~ "My company doesn't/I don't install any heat pumps, but will do so in the next 12 months",
                             x14_all == "My company doesn't install any heat pumps, and has no plans to do so" ~ "My company doesn't/I don't install any heat pumps, and has/have no plans to do so",
                             x14_all == "I don't install any heat pumps, but I plan to do so in the next 12 months" ~ "My company doesn't/I don't install any heat pumps, but will do so in the next 12 months",
                             x14_all == "I don't install any heat pumps and have no plans to do so" ~ "My company doesn't/I don't install any heat pumps, and has/have no plans to do so"))
data$x14_all <- as.factor(data$x14_all)




# Recoding for Qs 21a, 21b and 21c
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x21a_bis = case_when(x21a_is_your_business_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
                              x21a_is_your_business_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "No, we were previously MCS certified but the Nominated Technical Person has left the firm" ~ "Previously MCS certified",
                              x21a_is_your_business_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "No, we were previously MCS certified but decided to cease to be so" ~ "Previously MCS certified",
                              x21a_is_your_business_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "No, we have never been MCS certified" ~ "No, never been MCS certified",
                              x21a_is_your_business_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "Not yet, but we're in the process of certification" ~ "Not yet, but in the process of certification"))
data$x21a_bis <- as.factor(data$x21a_bis)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(x21b_bis = case_when(x21b_are_you_personally_registered_as_an_mcs_certified_heat_pump_installer == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
                              x21b_are_you_personally_registered_as_an_mcs_certified_heat_pump_installer == "I was previously MCS certified but decided to cease to be so" ~ "Previously MCS certified",
                              x21b_are_you_personally_registered_as_an_mcs_certified_heat_pump_installer == "No, I have never been MCS certified" ~ "No, never been MCS certified",
                              x21b_are_you_personally_registered_as_an_mcs_certified_heat_pump_installer == "Not yet, but I'm in the process of certification" ~ "Not yet, but in the process of certification"))
data$x21b_bis <- as.factor(data$x21b_bis)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(x21c_bis = case_when(x21c_is_the_firm_you_work_for_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "Yes" ~ "Yes",
                              x21c_is_the_firm_you_work_for_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "No, it was previously MCS certified but decided to cease to be so" ~ "Previously MCS certified",
                              x21c_is_the_firm_you_work_for_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "No, it was previously MCS certified but the Nominated Technical Person has left the firm" ~ "Previously MCS certified",
                              x21c_is_the_firm_you_work_for_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "No, it has never been MCS certified" ~ "No, never been MCS certified",
                              x21c_is_the_firm_you_work_for_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "Not yet, but it is in the process of certification" ~ "Not yet, but in the process of certification",
                              x21c_is_the_firm_you_work_for_mcs_certified_for_heat_pump_installations == "Don't know" ~ "Don't know"))
data$x21c_bis <- as.factor(data$x21c_bis)

# Merge Qs 21a, 21b and 21c
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x21a_bis = recode(x21a_bis, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x21b_bis = recode(x21b_bis, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x21c_bis = recode(x21c_bis, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(x21_all = coalesce(x21a_bis, x21b_bis, x21c_bis))


## Company owners
data$x22a_answer1 <- sapply(data$x22a_which_heat_pump_technologies_is_your_business_mcs_certified_to_install_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x22a_answer2 <- sapply(data$x22a_which_heat_pump_technologies_is_your_business_mcs_certified_to_install_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_airsource_MCS_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x22a_answer1, fixed("Air source heat pumps")) |
                                      str_detect(x22a_answer2, fixed("Air source heat pumps")), 1, NA_character_)) # 93 installers (all of them, those who are MCS certified)

# Do the same for New build
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_groundsource_MCS_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x22a_answer1, fixed("Ground or water source heat pumps")) |
                                      str_detect(x22a_answer2, fixed("Ground or water source heat pumps")), 1, NA_character_)) 

## Sole traders and contractors
data$x22b_answer1 <- sapply(data$x22b_which_heat_pump_technologies_are_you_mcs_certified_to_install_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x22b_answer2 <- sapply(data$x22b_which_heat_pump_technologies_are_you_mcs_certified_to_install_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_airsource_MCS_traders = ifelse(str_detect(x22b_answer1, fixed("Air source heat pumps")) |
                                              str_detect(x22b_answer2, fixed("Air source heat pumps")), 1, NA_character_))

### Questions 30a and 30b
## Installers were asked if they have done any retrofit or new build (select all that apply format)
## Some responded only retrofit, other only new build, others both.
## Those who replied retrofit and new build were asked q33, what is the majority of your installations.
## To create a binary variable retrofit_newbuild we want to include those who only responded retrofit to q30 and those who responded retrofit to q33.

## Filter the "only retrofit answers"
## To do this, I find answers which contain "retrofit" which include those who replied "retrofit" and "retrofit, new build".

# Separate vector
data$x30a_answer1 <- sapply(data$x30a_has_your_business_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x30a_answer2 <- sapply(data$x30a_has_your_business_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))

# Step 1
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_retrofit_q30a = ifelse(str_detect(x30a_answer1, fixed("Retrofit")) |
                                      str_detect(x30a_answer2, fixed("Retrofit")), 1, 0)) 

## I now have a dummy variable that takes the value 1 if respondents replied "retrofit" or "retrofit" and "new build" to q30a.

## Then I create a new variable with condition 1 = retrofit in new variable and condition 2 = not asked (q33) since those who replied only retrofit to q30 were not asked q33.
## This way I have a binary variable which takes the value "retrofit" for installers who replied "retrofit" only to q30.
## This follows the guidelines in the pre-analysis plan.

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_only_owners = case_when(dummy_retrofit_q30a == 1 & x33a_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_the_heat_pump_installations_your_business_has_done_been == "Not asked" ~ "Retrofit only", TRUE ~ NA_character_))
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value "retrofit only" for the respondent who only do retrofit work.

## I now do the same thing for newbuild
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_newbuild_q30a = ifelse(str_detect(x30a_answer1, fixed("New build")) |
                                      str_detect(x30a_answer2, fixed("New build")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(newbuild_only_owners = case_when(dummy_newbuild_q30a == 1 & x33a_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_the_heat_pump_installations_your_business_has_done_been == "Not asked" ~ "Newbuild only", TRUE ~ NA_character_))

## Now I create a summary variable with three levels: retrofit only, newbuild only, and both retrofit and newbuild.

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_newbuild_owners = case_when(retrofit_only_owners == "Retrofit only" ~ "Retrofit only",
                                              newbuild_only_owners == "Newbuild only" ~ "New build only",
                                              x30a_answer1 == "Not asked" ~ NA_character_,
                                              TRUE ~ "Both retrofit and new build"))
data$retrofit_newbuild_owners <- as.factor(data$retrofit_newbuild_owners)

## Now I repeat the same process for sole traders, employees and contractors.

data$x30b_answer1 <- sapply(data$x30b_have_you_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x30b_answer2 <- sapply(data$x30b_have_you_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_retrofit_q30b = ifelse(str_detect(x30b_answer1, fixed("Retrofit")) |
                                      str_detect(x30b_answer2, fixed("Retrofit")), 1, 0)) 

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_only_others = case_when(dummy_retrofit_q30b == 1 & x33b_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_your_heat_pump_installation_work_been == "Not asked" ~ "Retrofit only", TRUE ~ NA_character_))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_newbuild_q30b = ifelse(str_detect(x30b_answer1, fixed("New build")) |
                                      str_detect(x30b_answer2, fixed("New build")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>%
```

### Functions

```{r}
## Create a function to plot for all installers
create_plot_all_installers <- function(data, variable, title) {
  
  ggplot(data, aes(x = !!sym(variable))) +
    geom_bar(fill = "blue") +
    geom_text(stat='count', aes(label=after_stat(count)), vjust=-0.5, size = 3) + 
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = "Count") +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 20)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 20), limits = levels_order)
}


## Create function to get summary table
generate_table <- function(data, variable1, variable2) {
  table_result <- xtabs(~ data[[variable1]] + data[[variable2]], data)
  table_result <- as.data.frame.matrix(table_result)
  table_result$total_row <- rowSums(table_result)
  column_totals <- colSums(table_result, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_row <- as.data.frame(t(column_totals))
  row_name <- "total_col"
  rownames(total_row)[1] <- row_name
  table_result <- rbind(table_result, total_row)
}


## Create function to export all data frames in CSV
export_to_csv <- function(data_frame, file_name) {
  write.csv(data_frame, file_name, row.names = TRUE)
}


## Create a function to plot the distribution by employment type
create_plot_employ <- function(data, variable, title) {
  
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = variable, y = "count", fill = "employment_type")) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = "Count", fill = "Employment type") +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 20)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 16), limits = levels_order) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
}


## Create a function to plot (dodge) the distribution by employment type
create_plot_employ_dodge <- function(data, variable, title) {
  
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = variable, y = "count", fill = "employment_type")) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(count > 0, as.character(count), "0")),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = "Count", fill = "Employment type") +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 10)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 16), limits = levels_order) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
}


## Create a function to create data frame (employment type)
create_df_two <- function(data, variable1, variable2) {
  data %>% 
    drop_na({{ variable1 }}, {{ variable2 }}) %>%
    count({{ variable1 }}, {{ variable2 }}) %>%
    rename(count = n)
}


## Create a function to plot (dodge) the distribution by employment type
create_plot_dodge <- function(data, variable1, variable2, fill_label, title) {
  
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = variable1, y = "count", fill = variable2)) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(count > 0, as.character(count), "0")),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = "Count", fill = fill_label) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 10)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 14), limits = levels_order) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")
}


## Create a function to plot (dodge) the distribution by employment type
create_plot_dodge_zissou <- function(data, variable1, variable2, fill_label, title) {
  
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = variable1, y = "count", fill = variable2)) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(count > 0, as.character(count), "0")),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = "Count", fill = fill_label) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 10)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 16), limits = levels_order) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
}


## Create a function to create data frame
create_df <- function(data, variable) {
  data %>% 
    drop_na({{ variable }}) %>%
    count({{ variable }}) %>%
    rename(count = n)
}


## Create a function to create data frame (employment type)
create_df_employ <- function(data, variable) {
  data %>% 
    drop_na({{ variable }}, employment_type) %>%
    count({{ variable }}, employment_type) %>%
    rename(count = n)
}
```

#### 1.08 | Where are survey participants located in the UK?

Figure 1.8A shows the distribution of location by employment type. The graph shows the distribution for all installers (n=345). Note however that some installers selected multiple options, therefore the total count is greater than 345:

-   3 installers selected "England" and "Wales"

-   4 installers selected "England" and "Scotland"

-   2 installers selected "England", "Scotland", and "Wales"

```{r}
# Create a new data frame with only the dummy variables above
subset_dummy <- data %>%
  select(dummy_england, dummy_scotland, dummy_wales, dummy_northern_ireland, dummy_uk_wide, dummy_not_in_uk, dummy_dont_know, employment_type)

# Summarise the distribution
plot_1.8A <- subset_dummy %>%
  group_by(employment_type) %>%
  summarise_all(~ sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE))

# Add totals row
plot_1.8A <- plot_1.8A %>%
  mutate(total_row = rowSums(across(-1)))

# Add totals column
totals_row <- plot_1.8A %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(employment_type = "total_col")
plot_1.8A <- bind_rows(plot_1.8A, totals_row)

# Rename variables in the summary_table
new_names <- c("Employment type",
               "England", 
               "Scotland",
               "Wales",
               "Northern Ireland",
               "UK-wide business",
               "I don't work in the UK", 
               "Don't know",
               "total_row")

# Rename variables in the subset for clear display in plot
plot_1.8A <- plot_1.8A %>%
  rename_all(~ new_names)

# Export csv
export_to_csv(plot_1.8A, "plot_1.8A.csv")

# Subset by employment type to select company owners and sole traders
subset_q8 <- data %>% 
  select(dummy_england, dummy_scotland, dummy_wales, dummy_northern_ireland, dummy_uk_wide, dummy_not_in_uk, dummy_dont_know, employment_type)

# Summarise the distribution
summary_table <- subset_q8 %>%
  group_by(employment_type) %>%
  summarise_all(~ sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE))

# Rename variables in the summary_table
colnames(summary_table) <- c("Employment type",
                            "England", 
                            "Scotland",
                            "Wales",
                            "Northern Ireland",
                            "UK-wide business",
                            "I don't work in the UK", 
                            "Don't know")

# Reshape the data for ggplot
summary_long <- summary_table %>%
  gather(variable, count, -`Employment type`)

order_labels <- c("England", 
                  "Scotland",
                  "Wales",
                  "Northern Ireland",
                  "UK-wide business",
                  "I don't work in the UK", 
                  "Don't know")

# Create plot
ggplot(summary_long, aes(x = factor(variable, levels = order_labels), y = count, fill = `Employment type`)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Figure 1.8A. Distribution of work location by employment type (all installers)",
       x = "",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Employment type") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 260, by = 20)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
```

#### 2.03 | Are survey participants planning to change the proportion of their domestic or commercial heating work?

We also want to know whether installers plan to change the proportion of commercial and domestic works. To do this, we crossed the answers for the questions about current and future heating work to create a new binary variable that takes the values 1 if change and 0 otherwise. Figure 2.3A shows the distribution for all installers.

```{r}
# Create new binary variable to identify if change between current and future work
data <- data %>%
  mutate(change_heating_work = ifelse(x12_all != x13_all, "Change", "No change"))
data$change_heating_work <- as.factor(data$change_heating_work)

# Create data frame
plot_2.3A <- create_df(data, change_heating_work)

# Plot distribution
levels_order <- c("Change", "No change")

create_plot_all_installers(data = data, 
            variable = "change_heating_work", 
            title = "2.3A. Change between current and future work (all installers)")

# Export csv
export_to_csv(plot_2.3A, "plot_2.3A.csv")
```

#### 3.04 | Of those who are MCS certified, what types of heat pump are they certified to install?

For the installers who are MCS certified, we want to know which technologies. Only installers who answered that they are MCS certified were asked that question: 93 company owners, 8 sole traders or contractors, and 96 employees.

Figure 3.4A shows the distribution for all installers who have MCS certification or wok for companies which are MCS-certified by employment type (n=197). In this case, all company owners who are MCS certified are so for air source heat pumps. Therefore, the number of installers who selected ground or water source refers to installers who are certified for both types.

```{r}
# Select variables
subset_dummy <- data %>%
  select(x22_airsource_all, x22_groundsource_all, employment_type)

# Summarise the distribution
plot_3.4A <- subset_dummy %>%
  group_by(employment_type) %>%
  summarise_all(~ sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE))

# Add totals row
plot_3.4A <- plot_3.4A %>%
  mutate(total_row = rowSums(across(-1)))

# Add totals column
totals_row <- plot_3.4A %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(employment_type = "total_col")
plot_3.4A <- bind_rows(plot_3.4A, totals_row)

# Rename variables in the summary_table
new_names <- c("Employment type",
               "Air source heat pumps", 
               "Ground or water source heat pumps",
               "total_row")

# Rename variables in the subset for clear display in plot
plot_3.4A <- plot_3.4A %>%
  rename_all(~ new_names)

# Export csv
export_to_csv(plot_3.4A, "plot_3.4A.csv")

# Plot distribution
subset_plot <- data %>% 
  select(x22_airsource_all, x22_groundsource_all, employment_type)

# Summarise the distribution
summary_table <- subset_plot %>%
  group_by(employment_type) %>%
  summarise_all(~ sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE))

# Rename variables in the summary_table
new_names <- c("employment_type",
               "Air source heat pumps", 
               "Ground or water source heat pumps")

# Rename variables in the subset for clear display in plot
summary_table <- summary_table %>%
  rename_all(~ new_names)

# Reshape the data for ggplot
summary_long <- summary_table %>%
  gather(variable, count, -employment_type)

order_labels <- c("Air source heat pumps", "Ground or water source heat pumps")

# Plot
ggplot(summary_long, aes_string(x = "variable", y = "count", fill = "employment_type")) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(count > 0, as.character(count), "0")),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
    labs(title = "Figure 3.4A. Distribution of type of MCS-certified tech by employment type \n(all installers who are certified)", x = "", y = "Count", fill = "Employment type") +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 10)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 14)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
```

#### 3.14 | What barriers discourage survey participants from getting MCS certification?

Next, we combine answers for installers(company owners, sole traders and contractors) who have never been MCS certified and those who used to but no longer want to be MCS certified to get a clear idea of the existing barriers which discourage installers from obtaining MCS certification.

To do so we merged the following survey questions: 25a, 25b, 25c and 29. Figure 3.14A shows the distribution (n=94).

```{r}
# Merge corresponding pairs
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_expensive_merged = coalesce(dummy_expensive_all, dummy_too_expensive))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_paperwork_merged = coalesce(dummy_paperwork_all, dummy_too_much_paperwork))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_training_merged = coalesce(dummy_training_all, dummy_training))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_no_retrofit_merged = coalesce(dummy_no_retrofit_all, dummy_no_retrofit))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_alt_merged = coalesce(dummy_alt_all, dummy_prefer_umbrella_scheme))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_no_MCS_merged = coalesce(dummy_no_MCS_all, dummy_prefer_no_MCS))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_other_merged = coalesce(dummy_other_all, dummy_other))

# Select dummy variables
subset_dummy <- data %>%
  filter(employment_type != "Employee") %>% 
  select(dummy_expensive_merged,
         dummy_paperwork_merged,
         dummy_training_merged,
         dummy_no_retrofit_merged,
         dummy_alt_merged,
         dummy_no_MCS_merged,
         dummy_other_merged)

plot_3.14A <- subset_dummy %>%
  mutate_all(as.factor) %>% 
  summarise_all(~ sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE))

# Rename variables in the summary_table
new_names <- c("It is too expensive", 
               "There is too much paperwork", 
               "There is too much required training", 
               "My company doesn’t work in retrofit", 
               "Umbrella scheme or sign off from another organisation", 
               "I prefer to do retrofit outside the MCS scheme", 
               "Other")

# Create data frame to produce the table
plot_3.14A <- data.frame(dummy_variable = new_names, count = as.vector(t(plot_3.14A)))

# Export csv
export_to_csv(plot_3.14A, "plot_3.14A.csv")

# Produce plot
ggplot(plot_3.14A, aes(x = factor(dummy_variable, levels = c("It is too expensive", 
               "There is too much paperwork", 
               "There is too much required training", 
               "My company doesn’t work in retrofit", 
               "Umbrella scheme or sign off from another organisation", 
               "I prefer to do retrofit outside the MCS scheme", 
               "Other")), y = count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "blue") +
  geom_text(stat ='identity', aes(label = count), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "Figure 3.14A. Distribution of the reasons why installers (excluding employees) \nchoose not to be MCS certified", x = "", y = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 70, by = 10)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 12))
```

```{r}
# Rename variables in the subset for clear display in plot
summary_table <- summary_table %>%
  rename_all(~ new_names)

# Reshape the data for ggplot
summary_long <- summary_table %>%
  gather(variable, count, -x37_all)

levels_order <- c("My firm’s MCS certification",
                  "Umbrella scheme or sign off from another organisation",
                  "Without MCS certification",
                  "Other",
                  "Don't know")

# Plot
ggplot(summary_long, aes_string(x = "variable", y = "count", fill = "x37_all")) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(count > 0, as.character(count), "")),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    labs(title = "Figure 5.7B. Distribution of the number of installations in the past 12 months by the \nmethods that they use to MCS-certify their installations (medium and large companies)", x = "", y = "Count", fill = "Number of installations") +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 10)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 12), limits = levels_order) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")
```

#### 5.53| How does the number of heat pumps installed by survey participants differ depending on the distance they travel for work and the size of company they work for or own?

Note that contractors were not asked about company size. They are therefore not included here.

Figure 5.53A shows the distribution for sole traders (n=38).

```{r}
# Subset
data_subset <- data %>% 
  filter(size_company_owned_collapsed_2 == "Sole trader")

# Create data frame
plot_5.53A <- create_df_two(data_subset, distance_travelled_for_work_collapsed, x37_all_collapsed)

# Plot
levels_order <- c("Less than 25 miles", "25-50 miles", "50-100 miles", "Over 100 miles")
create_plot_dodge(data = plot_5.53A, 
                  variable1 = "distance_travelled_for_work_collapsed", 
                  variable2 = "x37_all_collapsed",
                  fill_label = "Number of installs",
                  title = "Figure 5.53A. Distribution of the number of heat pump installations in the past \n12 months by distance travelled for work (sole traders)")

# Create summary table
plot_5.53A <- generate_table(data_subset, "x37_all_collapsed", "distance_travelled_for_work_collapsed")

# Export csv
export_to_csv(plot_5.53A, "plot_5.53A.csv")
```
